title: FLORA HIGH SCHOOL HOMECOMING
full_story:
Flora High School is gearing up for Homecoming week which will start Dress up days.

Monday, September 21st will be Movie Star Monday, where students will dress as their favorite movie star.  Tuesday, September 22nd will be Something you Can’t Wear Anywhere Else day.  Wednesday, September 23rd will be Color War Day, Seniors will wear black, Juniors will wear yellow, Sophomores will wear Red, and Freshmen will wear Green.  Faculty will be dressed in Blue.  Thursday, September 24th will be Dolly Parton Day and Pink Out Day. and Friday, September 25th will be Crazy Orange and Blue Day.

The Homecoming Parade will be held Wednesday night, September 23rd beginning at 7:30 pm through downtown Flora.  The parade will start at the Depot with line up at 7, and end at the corner of North Avenue and Mill Street.  Class Competitions will then be held on Dancey Field at 8 with the bonfire to follow.

Friday night, September 25th, at 7 pm will be the Homecoming Football game at Dancey Field, against the Eldorado Eagles with the Homecoming court announced during half time of the game.

The student body has chosen the Queen candidates of Myra Sloan, Marli Myers, Qynlin Brown, Danica Conklin and Rosalyn Stanford.  King Candidates are Guy Arnold, Rylan Billingsly, Kehlin Crawford, Brennan O’Donnell, and Kormik Massie.  The Junior Class attendants are Morgan Irmen, Mylea Jones, Kennedy Zimmerman, Tyler Earnst, Braxton Oestrich, and Ashton Williams.  The Sophomores Class attendants are Vayda Kohn and Carson Smith.  The Freshmen Class Attendants are Halle Patridge and Sawyer Murbarger.

The coronation of the King and Queen will be held Saturday night, September 26th in the FHS Gym.  Dance opens at 7 for students, parents are welcome to enter at 7:15, coronation begins at 7:30 and dance is from 8 to 10 pm.

title: STAUDER NAMED OD OF YEAR
full_story:
Dr. Paul Stauder, OD, of the Precision EyeCare Center has been named recipient of the 2026 Illinois Optometrist of the Year award.

Dr. Stauder attended the University of Illinois from 1991 to 1994 before earning his Doctor of Optometry degree from Illinois College of Optometry in 1998.  Following graduation, Paul moved to Fairfield, where he purchased a practice from his brother, Dr. Scott Wooley.  He continues to practice full-scope primary care optometry there today.  More recently, Paul purchased a second location in Flora from Scott as his brother began transitioning into semi-retirement.

Paul is a past president of the Southern Illinois Optometric Society and was recognized as the IOA Young Optometrist of the Year in 2007.  He went on to serve as President of the Illinois Optometric Association in 2014–2015.

Today, he serves as Chair of the IOA PAC Board and remains actively engaged in advocacy as a state and federal key person for several legislators.  Paul has long believed that optometrists have a responsibility to be engaged in protecting and advancing their profession.

title: FORD TOWN FUN FEST 2026
full_story:
Ford Town Fun Fest is Friday, September 18th and Saturday, September 19th.

The location for the festival is in front of the Flora Public Library and Food trucks will be set up on East 2nd Street.

The event starts with a Cruise in Friday from 5 pm, starting at the parking lot of Beck’s Auto Sales with dash plaques to the first 100 entries.  The car show is open to any make or model of car.  They will be cruising through town and past Heritage Woods so the residents can look at the vehicles.  Food trucks inflatables and family yard games will be available at Library Park from 5 to 8 pm, and Just for Spite Unplugged will be playing from 6 to 9 pm.

Saturday the Clay County Cruisers will have a Car Show with registration from 9 until Noon.  The car show registration is $15 and there will be awards for the top 75 plus 5 specialty awards.  For Car show information call 618-676-4005, 618-662-5646 or 618-676-7732.  Dash plaques will be given to the first 100 entrants.  Craft and food vendors, inflatables, and games will also open at 9 am.  There are also commemorative T-shirts available for $20.

At noon the craft brew and chili cookoff sampling will begin and the dunking booth will open.  Car show awards are at 3 pm and craft beer and chili judging will begin at 4 pm.  So far there are 7 entries in the craft brew contest and 6 entries in the Chili Cookoff, with entries still being taken.  The winner of the Chili Cookoff will win a $100 gift card and have their name engraved on the Chili Cookoff Plaque in City Hall.  For more information call Arriel at the Chamber Office at 618-662-5646.

title: LIHEAP AVAILABLE
full_story:
CEFS Economic Opportunity Corp, as administrator of the Energy Assistance Program in the counties of Clay, Christian, Effingham, Fayette, Montgomery, Moultrie and Shelby announced that funds are available to assist income-eligible households with their natural gas, propane and/or electric bills and furnace assistance for inoperable heating systems.

The program will begin taking applications on October 1st, for older adults, age 60 and over, individuals with a disability, families with children age 5 years and under, and households that are disconnected from their utilities, have a disconnection notice or have less than 25% in their propane tank.  All other income eligible households can start applying November 2nd.

Applications will be taken on a first-come, first-served basis through August 13th, of 2027, or until funding is exhausted.  Households that receive a one-time benefit may return during the program year for a Reconnection Assistance or Furnace Assistance benefits, if needed.

The program has expanded eligibility this year.  Households that are customers of Ameren Illinois, Liberty Utilities, City of Flora, Village of Louisville, Village of Clay City or Shelby Electric must be at or below 300% of the Federal Poverty Guidelines to receive a benefit from LIHEAP.

The monthly income guidelines are as follows, one person can make up to $3,990 a month, two people can make up to $5,410, three people can make up to $6,830, and four people can make up to $8,250.

Households that are customers of all other utilities/energy vendors must be at or below 60% of the State Median Income to receive a benefit from LIHEAP.  The income guidelines for that are as follows, one person can make up to $3,441 a month, two people can make up to $4,500, three people can make up to $5,558, and four people can make up to $6,617.

Go to www.cefseoc.org or liheapillinois.com for the income limits for households with 5 members and more.

The Low-Income Home Energy Assistance Program (LIHEAP) provides one-time benefits to income eligible homeowners and renters to help with energy bills and for reconnection of energy service.

The following documentation is required for all applications; Proof of gross income from all household members for the prior 30-day period beginning with the date of application.  For all customers new to LIHEAP, and/or for new household members of previous customers, proof of Social Security numbers (SSN) for all household members.  Individuals without an SSN or Individual Taxpayer Identification Number (ITIN) can still apply and CEFS Outreach offices will advise accordingly.  A copy of current heat and electric bills issued within the last 30 days.  Cash assistance is available for renters who can provide a copy of their lease/rental agreement showing their heating costs are included in the rent.  Other documents may be needed based on your household situation.  If you have questions regarding this, please call the office.

Starting on September 21st appointments can be made by contacting the CEFS Clay County Outreach office at 835 West North Street in Flora the phone number is 618-662-4024.  The office is open Monday through Friday 8:30 am to 4:30 pm.

In order that no one is denied the opportunity to make an application we will continue to take applications in person or by phone.  Required documentation can be submitted in-person, mail or electronically.  If you require any special accommodation, please contact the local CEFS Outreach office in your county to arrange.

Income eligible LIHEAP customers of Ameren Illinois will receive a monthly discount on their natural and/or electric bill through the Low-Income Discount Rates.  Visit powerbilldiscount.com to know more details.

title: CROP PROGRESS AND CONDITION
full_story:
In its first corn harvest estimate of the season, USDA pegged progress in Illinois at 3% complete as of September 6th, compared to 2% a year ago and the five-year average of 1%.  The department estimates 29% of the state’s corn crop is mature and 24% of soybeans are dropping leaves, both slightly ahead of the average pace.

There were 6.8 days suitable for fieldwork in the week ending September 6th.  Statewide, the average temperature was 82.8 degrees, 12.4 degrees above normal.  Precipitation averaged .02 inches, 0.68 inches below normal.  Topsoil moisture supply was rated 9% very short, 30% short, 58% adequate, and 3% surplus.  Subsoil moisture supply was rated 10% very short, 29% short, 59% adequate, and 2% surplus.

Corn dough reached 96%, compared to the 5-year average of 94%.  Corn dented reached 76%, compared to the 5-year average of 78%.  Corn mature reached 29%, compared to the 5-year average of 27%.  Corn harvested reached 3% compared top the 5-year average of 1%.  Corn condition was rated 4% very poor, 9% poor, 32% fair, 42% good, and 13% excellent.

Soybeans dropping leaves reached 24%, compared to the 5-year average of 19%.  Soybeans condition was rated 5% very poor, 7% poor, 31% fair, 44% good, and 13% excellent.

title: AVIATION EXPO RETURNS
full_story:
Aviation enthusiasts, pilots, prospective aircraft owners and anyone curious about the world of flight are invited to the Mt. Vernon Outland Airport (MVN) for the 18th Annual Midwest Aviation Expo (MAX), taking place through Saturday, from 9 am to 4 pm daily.

Admission, parking, and local shuttles are all free, making the expo an accessible opportunity for visitors of all ages to experience aviation up close.

Over the past 18 years, the Midwest Aviation Expo has grown into a highly anticipated event at Mt. Vernon Outland Airport, bringing aircraft manufacturers, aviation professionals, pilots and visitors together in Southern Illinois.

Throughout the three-day expo, aircraft will be flying all day, every day, giving attendees the chance to see a diverse collection of MOSAIC aircraft, Light Sport Aircraft (LSAs) and ultralights in action.  Demonstration flights and static aircraft displays will provide additional opportunities to get a closer look at today’s recreational aviation industry.

title: JOHNSONVILLE RURITAN FALL HUNT
full_story:
The Johnsonville Ruritan Club will have their third annual adult Fall Egg Hunt Saturday, October 3rd. The evening will start with a meal at 5 pm that will cost $10.  The menu is chicken and noodles, mashed potatoes, green beans, hot rolls and desserts.  There will be to-go containers available.  There will also be a 50/50 raffle.  Everyone is welcome to the meal.

Registration for the hunt starts at 6:30 pm and the hunt will start at dark, cost is $20 per ticket and the hunt is open to those 18 and older.  Adults are welcome to bring a flashlight so they can hunt in the dark throughout marked areas in Johnsonville for an allotted amount of time.  Participants will collect as many eggs as possible for a chance to win prizes.  Prizes are being donated by area businesses.  People who want to participate can buy their tickets for the hunt in advance at The Village Florist in Cisne or online at runsignup.com.

title: ILLINOIS STATE PUBLIC DEFENDER
full_story:
The Illinois Supreme Court invites applications from individuals interested in serving as the initial Illinois State Public Defender, a new chief executive role overseeing an independent agency within the Judicial Branch.  In this role, the selected individual will be the State’s leading advocate for Illinois’ public defenders and for the constitutional rights of people charged with offenses and represented by Illinois’ public defense system.  The State Public Defender will also establish policies, practices, resources, and reforms necessary to ensure effective and meaningful representation of defendants across Illinois.

Applications will be accepted until Friday, October 9th.  Submitted applications will be reviewed prior to selecting finalists, after which the Illinois Supreme Court will appoint an initial State Public Defender for a two-year term beginning January 1st.

The State Public Defender will be responsible for establishing, supervising, and administering a statewide public defense system that ensures constitutionally required legal representation for indigent persons in criminal, juvenile delinquency, and dependency matters.  The individual hired will oversee the buildout of the office, the installation of the infrastructure, the implementation of statutory guidelines, and will identify the funding sources, hire key leadership and locate and position regional offices.  The State Public Defender must devote full time to the duties of the office and may not engage in the private practice of law.  The annual salary of $218,400 is established by statute.

The minimum qualifications for the position are being a licensed attorney in good standing in Illinois, at least 5 years of licensed practice, evidence of administrative and supervisory experience, evidence of experience representing persons accused of crime, and evidence of dedication to high-quality indigent defense and a plan to improve statewide defense services.

For more information contact James Brunner, Public Information Officer of the Illinois Supreme Court at 217-208-3354 or [email protected].
